lessons.title: Guess the character from the line
lessons.description: Trade samurai, ninja and elder lines in a guessing game with friends.
lessons.canDo: Follow the meaning of stylised ぜ/ぞ and recognise a performed character.

lessons.title: Play through the gate scene
lessons.description: Read a little fantasy scene, then discuss the cliffhanger.
lessons.canDo: Understand wondering, explanation and older copulas in a short character scene.

grammar.title: Read a bundle of character cues
grammar.formation: Pronoun/form of address + predicate + sentence ending. Recognise わし/拙者 in labelled fictional roles; identify the actual speaker from the scene.
grammar.explanation: Fiction often bundles pronouns, address forms and endings to suggest a role. わし with じゃ can signal a stylised elder; 拙者 with でござる can signal a stylised samurai. These are recognition cues, not proof of a real person’s age, gender or occupation. One actor can perform several roles. Dialect is a real variety, not incorrect Japanese.
grammar.example: 「わしは道を知っておる」と、老人の役が言う。
grammar.translation: The elder role says, “I know the way.”

examples.ja: 「わしは{道|みち}を{知|し}っておる」と、{老人|ろうじん}の{役|やく}が{言|い}う。
examples.en: The elder role says, “I know the way.”

examples.ja: 「{拙者|せっしゃ}は{門|もん}を{守|まも}る」と、{侍|さむらい}の{役|やく}が{言|い}う。
examples.en: The samurai role says, “I guard the gate.”

examples.ja: {配役|はいやく}を{見|み}ると、{両方|りょうほう}をケンタが{演|えん}じている。
examples.en: The casting shows Kenta performs both roles.

grammar.mistake: Do not answer who actually spoke just by the pronoun. Check the actor label and surrounding scene.

grammar.title: Recognise emphatic ぜ and ぞ
grammar.formation: Plain verb/i-adjective + ぜ/ぞ; noun/na-adjective + だぜ/だぞ. Volitional + ぜ can invite a shared action.
grammar.explanation: ぜ and ぞ add an emphatic, often assertive familiar delivery. They can announce an intention, reaction or warning. Fiction may use them to mark a forceful character, but they are not unique to villains or men. This unit practises understanding labelled script lines; teacher and workplace replies continue to use their appropriate register.
grammar.example: この手紙は俺が届けるぜ。
grammar.translation: I’ll deliver this letter, I tell you.

examples.ja: この{手紙|てがみ}は{俺|おれ}が{届|とど}けるぜ。
examples.en: I’ll deliver this letter, I tell you.

examples.ja: {門|もん}の{外|そと}は{危|あぶ}ないぞ。
examples.en: Outside the gate is dangerous, mind you.

examples.ja: この{町|まち}の{英雄|えいゆう}だぞ。
examples.en: That’s this town’s hero, you know.

grammar.mistake: Keep noun/na-adjective だ: 英雄だぞ. Do not infer an occupation from ぜ or change the underlying event meaning.

grammar.title: A marked style still carries a meaning
grammar.formation: Plain verb/i-adjective + わ; noun/na-adjective + だわ in the taught script pattern. Plain phrase + かしら; remove plain noun/na-adjective だ before かしら.
grammar.explanation: In a stylised character line, わ can add a marked delivery, while かしら expresses wondering. かしら often sounds feminine in contemporary media, but this is not a rule identifying an actual person. わ also occurs in different regional and casual styles with different intonation. Decode the whole line and context. This unit doesn’t score rising/falling intonation as a verified audio fact.
grammar.example: 門はまだ開いているかしら。
grammar.translation: I wonder whether the gate is still open.

examples.ja: {門|もん}はまだ{開|あ}いているかしら。
examples.en: I wonder whether the gate is still open.

examples.ja: この{手紙|てがみ}は{大切|たいせつ}だわ。
{今日|きょう}は{休|やす}みかしら。
examples.en: I wonder whether today is a day off.

grammar.mistake: かしら is wondering, not a guarantee or completed action. Do not add だ in the taught noun+かしら form or identify gender from わ alone.

grammar.title: のだ connects a statement to its context
grammar.formation: Plain V/i-adjective + のだ/んだ; affirmative noun/na-adjective + なのだ/なんだ. Polite のです/んです.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve the explanatory pattern to give a reason or interpretation connected to the situation. のだ is also common in prose; it’s not exclusively an anime or villain ending. Spoken んだ is normal Japanese. Affirmative nouns/na-adjectives require な, while negative じゃない attaches directly. Context supplies the explanatory link; のだ doesn’t make a mistaken claim true.
grammar.example: 道を知らない。初めてこの王国に来たのだ。
grammar.translation: I don’t know the way. The thing is, this is my first visit to this kingdom.

examples.ja: {道|みち}を{知|し}らない。{初|はじ}めてこの{王国|おうこく}に{来|き}たのだ。
examples.en: I don’t know the way. The thing is, this is my first visit to this kingdom.

examples.ja: {彼|かれ}は{勇者|ゆうしゃ}なのだ。だから{冒険|ぼうけん}に{出|で}る。
examples.en: He is the hero. That’s why he goes on the adventure.

examples.ja: {魔法|まほう}は{使|つか}えないんだ。
examples.en: The thing is, I cannot use magic.

grammar.mistake: 勇者なのだ requires な. のだ is explanatory, not an automatic cause marker like ので and not proof that a statement is factual.

grammar.title: Recognise two stylised older copulas
grammar.formation: Fictional elder: N/na-adjective + じゃ (=だ); V/i-adjective + のじゃ for explanatory のだ. Samurai: N/na-adjective + でござる (=である/です here).
grammar.explanation: In this script, noun + じゃ replaces the modern copula だ and noun + でござる creates an older samurai-style statement. A verb is not followed by the same でござる template: the taught noun phrase is 門番でござる. These forms are recognition only. じゃ also has real dialect uses; don’t label all users as elderly. Neither is the contraction じゃん or the negative じゃない.
grammar.translation: This is the kingdom’s gate. (stylised elder)

examples.ja: ここは{王国|おうこく}の{門|もん}じゃ。
examples.en: This is the kingdom’s gate. (stylised elder)

examples.ja: {拙者|せっしゃ}は{門番|もんばん}でござる。
この{道|みち}を{進|すす}むのじゃ。
examples.en: You are to follow this road. (stylised elder explanatory instruction)

grammar.mistake: Do not read じゃ as じゃない. Keep で in 門番でござる; recognise the quoted style without using it as a modern business-politeness model.

dialogues.title: A character-line guessing game
dialogues.scene: At home, Misaki, Kenta and Bao play a character-line guessing game. Kenta performs the samurai and elder; Misaki plays the princess; Bao plays the ninja. They use no costumes.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {前|まえ}は{早口|はやくち}の{語尾|ごび}を{聞|き}き{逃|のが}しちゃったね。{今日|きょう}は{短|みじか}い{台本|だいほん}で{遊|あそ}ぼうよ。
lines.romaji: Mae wa hayakuchi no gobi o kikinogashichatta ne. Kyō wa mijikai daihon de asobō yo.
lines.meaning: We missed those fast endings last time. Let’s play with a short script today.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: いいね。{僕|ぼく}は{侍|さむらい}と{老人|ろうじん}。ミサキは{姫|ひめ}で、バオは{忍者|にんじゃ}ね。
lines.romaji: Ii ne. Boku wa samurai to rōjin. Misaki wa hime de, Bao wa ninja ne.
lines.meaning: Sounds fun. I’ll do the samurai and the elder. Misaki, you’re the princess; Bao, you’re the ninja.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {仮装|かそう}はなしで、{台詞|せりふ}だけで{当|あ}てるんだね。じゃ、{先|さき}に{演|えん}じてみてよ。
lines.romaji: Kasō wa nashi de, serifu dake de ateru n da ne. Ja, saki ni enjite mite yo.
lines.meaning: No costumes—just guess from the lines? Go on, give us the first one.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {配役|はいやく}はメモしとくね。ケンタの{一人|ひとり}{二役|ふたやく}、{間違|まちが}えちゃいそう。
lines.romaji: Haiyaku wa memo shitoku ne. Kenta no hitori futayaku, machigaechaisō.
lines.meaning: I’ll note down the roles. I’m going to mix up Kenta’s two characters.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: 「{拙者|せっしゃ}は{門番|もんばん}でござる。ここは{通|とお}せぬ！」さて、{誰|だれ}でしょう？
lines.romaji: Sessha wa monban de gozaru. Koko wa tōsenu! Sate, dare deshō?
lines.meaning: “I’m the gatekeeper. You shall not pass!” So, who am I?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {侍|さむらい}！ じゃ、{次|つぎ}は{俺|おれ}ね。「この{手紙|てがみ}は{俺|おれ}が{届|とど}けるぜ。{任|まか}せとけ！」
lines.romaji: Samurai! Ja, tsugi wa ore ne. Kono tegami wa ore ga todokeru ze. Makasetoke!
lines.meaning: The samurai! My turn. “I’ll deliver this letter. Leave it to me!”

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {忍者|にんじゃ}だね。「ここは{町|まち}の{門|もん}じゃ。{夜|よる}には{閉|し}まるのじゃ」。これは{簡単|かんたん}かな？
lines.romaji: Ninja da ne. Koko wa machi no mon ja. Yoru ni wa shimaru no ja. Kore wa kantan kana?
lines.meaning: The ninja. “This is the town gate. It closes at night.” Is this one too easy?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {老人|ろうじん}！ 「じゃ」が{口癖|くちぐせ}みたい。{標準語|ひょうじゅんご}なら「ここは{町|まち}の{門|もん}だ」だね。
lines.romaji: Rōjin! Ja ga kuchiguse mitai. Hyōjungo nara koko wa machi no mon da da ne.
lines.meaning: The elder! “Ja” is like his catchphrase. In standard Japanese, that’s “This is the town gate.”

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {姫|ひめ}の{台詞|せりふ}も{聞|き}きたいな。{次|つぎ}の{場面|ばめん}、みんなで{朗読|ろうどく}しようよ。
lines.romaji: Hime no serifu mo kikitai na. Tsugi no bamen, minna de rōdoku shiyō yo.
lines.meaning: I want to hear the princess too. Let’s all read the next scene.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: じゃ、{今度|こんど}は{止|と}めずに{行|い}くぞ。{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}すところまでね。
lines.romaji: Ja, kondo wa tomezu ni iku zo. Tegami o watasu tokoro made ne.
lines.meaning: Okay, let’s go without stopping this time. Up to the part where we hand over the letter.

dialogues.title: A fictional gate; real actors
dialogues.scene: The friends read their assigned roles in a fantasy scene at a closed gate, then stop at the cliffhanger. The elder says to leave tomorrow; the ninja has not delivered the letter yet.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: 「{門|もん}はまだ{開|あ}いているかしら。{急|いそ}がなくてはいけないわ」。
lines.romaji: Mon wa mada aite iru kashira. Isoganakute wa ikenai wa.
lines.meaning: “I wonder if the gate’s still open. We must hurry.”

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: 「{門|もん}は{閉|し}まっておる。{冒険|ぼうけん}に{出|で}るのは{明日|あした}じゃ。{今夜|こんや}はここで{休|やす}むのじゃ」。
lines.romaji: Mon wa shimatte oru. Bōken ni deru no wa ashita ja. Kon’ya wa koko de yasumu no ja.
lines.meaning: “The gate is closed. We leave on our adventure tomorrow. Rest here tonight.”

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: 「ならば、{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}すまで{待|ま}つぞ。{朝|あさ}になったら、すぐ{出発|しゅっぱつ}するぜ」。
lines.romaji: Naraba, tegami o watasu made matsu zo. Asa ni nattara, sugu shuppatsu suru ze.
lines.meaning: “Then I’ll wait until I hand over the letter. At dawn, I’ll leave straight away.”

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: 「ありがとう。この{手紙|てがみ}は{大切|たいせつ}だわ。{王国|おうこく}の{運命|うんめい}がかかっているの」。
lines.romaji: Arigatō. Kono tegami wa taisetsu da wa. Ōkoku no unmei ga kakatte iru no.
lines.meaning: “Thank you. This letter is precious. The kingdom’s fate depends on it.”

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: 「おぬしは{勇者|ゆうしゃ}なのじゃ。{魔法|まほう}が{使|つか}えなくても、{道|みち}を{知|し}っておる」。
lines.romaji: Onushi wa yūsha na no ja. Mahō ga tsukaenakute mo, michi o shitte oru.
lines.meaning: “You are the hero. Even without magic, you know the road.”

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: 「{魔法|まほう}は{使|つか}えないのだ。だが、{手紙|てがみ}は{必|かなら}ず{届|とど}けるぞ！」…ここまで？
lines.romaji: Mahō wa tsukaenai no da. Daga, tegami wa kanarazu todokeru zo! Koko made?
lines.meaning: “I can’t use magic. But I’ll deliver the letter!” …Is that where we stop?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{結末|けつまつ}が{書|か}いてないじゃん。{続|つづ}き、どうなるのかな。
lines.romaji: Un. Ketsumatsu ga kaitenai jan. Tsuzuki, dō naru no kana.
lines.meaning: Yeah. There’s no ending written here! I wonder what happens next.

lines.speaker: Kenta
lines.line: {門番|もんばん}が{悪役|あくやく}だったりして。「{通|とお}すわけにはいかぬ！」とか。
lines.romaji: Monban ga akuyaku dattari shite. Tōsu wake ni wa ikanu! Toka.
lines.meaning: Maybe the gatekeeper’s the villain. “I cannot let you pass!” Something like that.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {怖|こわ}いなあ。{忍者|にんじゃ}はもう{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}したんだっけ？
lines.romaji: Kowai nā. Ninja wa mō tegami o watashita n da kke?
lines.meaning: That’s scary. Had the ninja handed over the letter yet?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: まだだよ。{次|つぎ}はその{場面|ばめん}の{前後|ぜんご}も{見|み}てみよう。{姫|ひめ}の{返事|へんじ}も{気|き}になるわ。
lines.romaji: Mada da yo. Tsugi wa sono bamen no zengo mo mite miyō. Hime no henji mo ki ni naru wa.
lines.meaning: Not yet. Next time, let’s watch what comes before and after that scene too. I’m curious about the princess’s reply.

readings.title: Misaki’s note after the guessing game
paragraphs: ケンタとバオへ。{今日|きょう}の{朗読|ろうどく}の{配役|はいやく}を{残|のこ}しておくね。ケンタが{侍|さむらい}と{老人|ろうじん}、バオが{忍者|にんじゃ}、{私|わたし}が{姫|ひめ}を{演|えん}じた。{仮装|かそう}はしていないけど、{台詞|せりふ}だけで{当|あ}てるのも{面白|おもしろ}かった。
{架空|かくう}の{王国|おうこく}の{門|もん}は{閉|し}まっていて、{冒険|ぼうけん}に{出|で}るのは{明日|あした}だと{老人|ろうじん}の{役|やく}が{言|い}った。{忍者|にんじゃ}は{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}すまで{待|ま}つと{言|い}っただけで、まだ{渡|わた}していない。{結末|けつまつ}はこの{台本|だいほん}には{書|か}いていない。
ケンタの{老人|ろうじん}の{口癖|くちぐせ}が{気|き}に{入|い}ったよ。{私|わたし}も「じゃ」を{言|い}ってみたくなっちゃった。{次|つぎ}の{視聴|しちょう}では{場面|ばめん}の{前後|ぜんご}も{聞|き}くね。{手紙|てがみ}を{受|う}け{取|と}った{姫|ひめ}は、どんな{返事|へんじ}をするのかな。ミサキ

glosses.text: 言ってみたくなっちゃった
glosses.kana: いってみたくなっちゃった
glosses.meaning: ended up wanting to try saying it

exercises.prompt: Which two roles does Kenta perform?
exercises.explain: Kenta explicitly assigns himself 侍と老人; Misaki and Bao have the other two roles.

exercises.prompt: How do they play the guessing game?
options: Guess the character from a line, without costumes
Guess only from the costume colour
exercises.explain: Bao says 仮装はなしで、台詞だけで当てる: no costumes, just guessing from the spoken lines.

exercises.prompt: Why did Misaki suggest reading a short script?
options: They missed fast endings in the earlier viewing
They had already completed the sequel
exercises.explain: Misaki says they missed fast endings last time and suggests playing with a short script.

exercises.context: Form practice: keep the noun copula before the named emphatic ending ぜ.
exercises.line: この{人物|じんぶつ}は{武士|ぶし}＿＿ぜ。
exercises.explain: Noun+だぜ keeps the noun copula before the emphatic ending.

exercises.context: Form practice: add the named emphatic ぞ directly to the plain verb, without a noun copula.
exercises.line: {侍|さむらい}が{手紙|てがみ}を{渡|わた}す＿＿。
exercises.explain: Plain verb+ぞ, not 渡すだぞ.

exercises.context: Your friend missed the meaning. Offer to rephrase in standard language and listen again.
exercises.line: {意味|いみ}を{聞|き}き{逃|のが}した。
options: {標準語|ひょうじゅんご}で{言|い}い{直|なお}して、もう{一度|いちど}{聞|き}こう。
{聞|き}き{逃|のが}したなら、もう{全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かったんだね。
{意味|いみ}は{気|き}にせず、{音量|おんりょう}だけ{見|み}よう。
exercises.explain: Rephrasing and replay respond to missed meaning; the others falsely assume understanding or dismiss it.

exercises.line: 「{拙者|せっしゃ}は{門番|もんばん}でござる。ここは{通|とお}せぬ！」さて、{誰|だれ}でしょう？
exercises.prompt: Who performs the gatekeeper’s line in this scene?
exercises.explain: Kenta performs this exact line, then invites the others to guess the character.

exercises.prompt: When does the fictional elder say the adventure begins?
exercises.explain: The elder says 冒険に出るのは明日じゃ and tells them to rest here tonight.

exercises.prompt: What does the ninja’s line establish about the letter?
options: He will wait until handing it over; it’s not yet delivered
exercises.explain: The ninja says he will wait until handing over the letter. Misaki later confirms he has not delivered it yet.

exercises.context: Form practice: attach the named wondering かしら to a noun without だ.
exercises.line: {明日|あした}の{朗読|ろうどく}はお{休|やす}み＿＿。
exercises.explain: 休み+かしら in this taught wondering pattern; it doesn’t assert the answer.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the named explanatory のだ after the affirmative noun 勇者.
exercises.line: {彼|かれ}は{勇者|ゆうしゃ}＿＿のだ。
exercises.explain: Affirmative noun+なのだ, not 勇者だのだ.

exercises.context: Recognition/form practice: complete the fictional elder’s positive noun statement with the named older copula じゃ.
exercises.line: ここは{王国|おうこく}の{門|もん}＿＿。
exercises.explain: Noun+じゃ is the stylised copula here. It’s neither affirmative じゃん nor negative じゃない.

exercises.context: You missed a cliffhanger. Ask to replay the surrounding scene to understand what happened.
exercises.line: {手紙|てがみ}、もう{渡|わた}したんだっけ？
options: {場面|ばめん}の{前後|ぜんご}も{聞|き}いて{確|たし}かめよう。
{手紙|てがみ}なんて{出|で}てこなかったよ。
{台本|だいほん}には{人物|じんぶつ}がいないよ。
exercises.explain: Replaying the surrounding scene addresses the missed action; the other replies contradict the script.

exercises.line: 「{門|もん}はまだ{開|あ}いているかしら。{急|いそ}がなくてはいけないわ」。
exercises.prompt: Who wonders whether the gate is open?
exercises.explain: Misaki performs the princess’s exact opening line.

exercises.meaning: The thing is, I cannot use magic. Use the explanatory のだ.
exercises.explain: The negative plain verb 使えない takes のだ directly; noun/na-adjective な is not used here.

exercises.prompt: Who performed the elder role in the casting notes?
exercises.explain: The first paragraph assigns Kenta both the samurai and elder roles.

exercises.prompt: According to the message, what is the delivery status?
options: The ninja has not handed over the letter yet
The elder has torn it up
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly says まだ渡していない.

exercises.prompt: What will Misaki check in the next viewing?
options: What comes before and after the scene
exercises.explain: The last paragraph says 場面の前後も聞く; the ending is not in the script.

watch.prompt: Optionally save a character line from your own clip. Note the literal message, role cue, actual speaker and surrounding action. Do not use fictional speech as a model for every real interaction.

recycling.reason: The character guessing game uses useful media words, without squeezing every previous-unit target into performed fantasy lines.
